name: Singapore
summary: Singapore publishes official UBL 2.1 examples (PINT-SG, the InvoiceNow profile of Peppol) and 19 Myinfo sandbox NRIC/FINs. However, every UEN in IMDA's examples fails its check letter, and some UENs in them, or their "corrected" forms, belong to real entities. The usable UENs here are therefore derived: they pass the check letter and were looked up in ACRA's full open register (2.1 million rows). Local company numbers use a past year whose serial range is closed, so they can never be issued. No authority reserves phone numbers, domains, postcodes or company numbers for fiction. Not obtained: the IRAS Check GST Register sandbox test data and the Myinfo v5 test personas. Postal sector 74 looks unused but was not exhaustively verified.

identifiers.name: UEN (Unique Entity Number)
identifiers.format: Business (ROB) nnnnnnnnX; local company (ROC) yyyynnnnnX; others [TSR]yyPQnnnnX
identifiers.authority: ACRA (and other issuing agencies for the "others" format)
identifiers.notes: ACRA does not publish the check-letter algorithms; the python-stdnum rules were verified against all 2.1 M ACRA records. Peppol endpoint value is SGUEN + UEN.

identifiers.name: GST registration number
identifiers.format: Usually the UEN; otherwise M + check character + 7 digits + check letter (10 characters, e.g. M2-1234567-K)
identifiers.notes: No public check algorithm for the M… format.

identifiers.name: NRIC / FIN
identifiers.format: S/T (citizens, PRs) or F/G/M (foreigners) + 7 digits + check letter
identifiers.notes: ICA does not publish the rule. The M series (FINs from 2022) uses a different table that was not verified.

identifiers.name: Postal code
identifiers.format: 6 digits; first two = postal sector (01–82), last four = delivery point (one code per building)
